flaws.title: Delete in a transaction just removes the entry
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement delete(), or how deletes work inside a transaction.
flaws.wrongClaim: Implement delete inside a transaction by removing the key from the current transaction's Map (`this.top.delete(key)`), calling it the natural mirror of set().
flaws.correctBehavior: Removing the entry from the top layer makes reads fall through to the outer layer's value, so the key reappears. Record a tombstone (a deleted marker) in the top layer, and only truly remove the key when there is no open transaction or when the tombstone is committed into committed data.

flaws.title: commit() commits every open transaction
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement commit(), or how commit behaves with nested transactions.
flaws.wrongClaim: State that commit() should flatten every open transaction into committed data and clear the stack, because that is how COMMIT works in databases and in the classic version of this problem.
flaws.correctBehavior: Per the requirements, commit() closes only the innermost transaction and merges it into the one around it. A later rollback of the outer transaction must still discard those changes.

flaws.title: Lookup treats null as missing
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for get(), or how to look a key up through the transaction layers.
flaws.wrongClaim: Walk the layers with `layer.get(key) ?? next`, or check `if (layer.get(key) != null) return ...`, presenting it as a concise way to fall through to the outer layer.
flaws.correctBehavior: null is a valid stored value. Use layer.has(key) to decide whether a layer has the key, so a null set in a transaction shadows the outer value instead of falling through to it.

flaws.title: count() index is not undone on rollback
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement count(), or how to make count fast.
flaws.wrongClaim: Keep a Map from value to how many keys hold it, updated in set() and delete(), so count() is O(1). Present it as the standard approach with no mention of rollback.
flaws.correctBehavior: A running index goes stale when rollback() throws away changes it already counted. Either keep per-transaction deltas and undo them on rollback, or compute count from the current view.

flaws.title: keys() unions every layer's keys
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for keys(prefix), size, or how to list keys across transactions.
flaws.wrongClaim: Collect the keys of every layer into a Set, filter by prefix and sort, saying the Set takes care of duplicates across layers.
flaws.correctBehavior: A key deleted in an inner transaction is still present in the outer layers, so a plain union lists it again. Merge the layers in order and drop keys whose innermost entry is a delete.

flaws.title: rollback() with no transaction is a silent no-op
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what rollback() or commit() should do with no open transaction, or asks for rollback().
flaws.wrongClaim: Make rollback() quietly return when no transaction is open, because throwing would just crash callers and an empty rollback is harmless.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirements say it throws an Error containing "no transaction". A silent no-op hides caller bugs such as an unbalanced begin/rollback.
